## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the NextItNet backbone through a family-specific `ModelView`. Structural inspection checks residual blocks, dilated temporal convolutions, normalization, masking and causal padding. When recognized, the prefix-mean gate extends potential dependence across the retained history. Backbone implementation is not supplied here, so structural conclusions remain conditional.

`log2feats(sequence)` returns per-position features. Final sequence representations use the **largest nonpadding index**, correctly handling left padding. `item_emb` supplies item vectors; `predict_score(features, items)` supplies scores.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, mapped training histories through `view.user_train`, and optional metadata. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` reads up to ten `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` batches of shape B × L. Probes run without gradients in evaluation mode; module modes and global random states are restored afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Training separation:** Positive-minus-negative margins, tenth percentile, error rate, margins below 0.5 and tie-adjusted pairwise accuracy. Larger positive separation indicates better sampled training discrimination; margins depend on score scale.
- **Representation geometry:** Item and endpoint norms, covariance spectra, effective rank and angular alignment describe concentration or degeneracy. They do not establish ranking quality.
- **User score sensitivity:** Up to 200 training users receive 99 fixed unseen training-observed candidates. Absolute and signed score changes measure dependence on history, without a universal desirable direction.

Checks cover repeatability, batch reordering, future-token causality, reachable offsets and leading-padding removal. Temporal interventions delete, zero, frequency-match replace or shuffle history regions at 25%/50% strengths. Geometry controls help distinguish content sensitivity from position changes.
